name: BrightPath CSM - Aligned
description: Aligned performance review. Customer Success Manager and Director of Customer Success largely agree on strong results, reliable execution, and good communication, with a small honest gap on enterprise negotiation growth.

answers.employee: I'm a Customer Success Manager at BrightPath Software, and during this quarter my performance should be evaluated against managing my portfolio of 40 mid-market accounts, driving renewals, reducing churn, and onboarding new customers. My main priorities were protecting at-risk renewals, improving product adoption, and coordinating with support and product teams on customer issues. Most of my time went to renewal conversations and adoption reviews. I also took on a temporary project leading a new onboarding playbook. My scope expanded slightly this quarter when two enterprise accounts were added to my book, which was a change from the prior period. One area that was a bit unclear was how much ownership I had over upsell targets versus the sales team.

answers.employee: The goals that mattered most were hitting a 92% renewal rate, keeping churn under 5%, and raising product adoption scores across my accounts. Success was measured by renewal percentage, churn rate, and adoption metrics in our customer health dashboard. These mattered because renewals are the core of our recurring revenue and churn directly affects company growth. The targets were communicated clearly in my quarterly plan and reviewed in our weekly one-on-ones, so I understood them well. The renewal and churn targets were formally assigned; the adoption improvement was more of an evolving priority that grew during the quarter.

answers.employee: I delivered a 94% renewal rate, beating my 92% target, and kept churn at 3.8%, under the 5% goal. I also raised average adoption scores in my portfolio by 12 points. These results mattered because they protected roughly $2.1M in recurring revenue and improved customer health going into next quarter. I personally led the save of two at-risk enterprise accounts by running tailored value reviews and pulling in product for a key feature request. My renewal and churn numbers exceeded expectations; adoption met expectations. The evidence is in the health dashboard and the renewal reports.

Renewal and churn results exceeded expectations; adoption met expectations. The evidence is in the health dashboard and renewal reports.

answers.employee: I followed through reliably on my commitments this quarter, hitting almost all my renewal deadlines and account review schedules. I took clear ownership of my at-risk accounts and proactively flagged two renewals that were trending down early enough to save them. My execution was consistent overall. One renewal was delayed because a customer had a budget freeze, and I escalated it early and kept my manager informed. I owned most of my work independently, only pulling in my manager for the largest enterprise negotiations.

answers.employee: The quality of my work was high and consistent. My account reviews were thorough and well-prepared, and my renewal proposals were accurate with no pricing errors this quarter. An example is the onboarding playbook I built, which the team adopted as a standard. Quality was consistent throughout the period. There were a couple of small instances where I had to redo a health report because of a data sync issue, but that was a tool problem, not a preparation issue. Good templates and our CRM tools supported the quality.

answers.employee: I communicated clearly and regularly with my manager through weekly one-on-ones and quick updates on urgent account risks. With peers, support, and product I collaborated through shared account channels and joint customer calls. Coordination through those channels worked well and helped me save at-risk accounts. Communication mostly helped my performance. The one friction point was occasional slow handoffs from the product team on feature requests, which sometimes delayed customer answers. A clearer product-request process would improve collaboration next period.

answers.employee: My judgment and adaptability grew this quarter, especially when I took on the two enterprise accounts and had to adjust my approach to larger, more complex customers. I applied feedback from my manager on running executive-level value reviews and got noticeably better at them. This growth improved my performance and shows I'm building toward handling a full enterprise book. The main development area that remains is deepening my commercial and negotiation skills for large deals. Coaching on enterprise negotiation and more exposure to renewals with procurement teams would help. I'd prioritize negotiation skills first.

answers.employee: One context factor is that I absorbed two enterprise accounts mid-quarter without a reduction in my existing book, so my workload increased. The product handoff delays I mentioned were an external constraint on some customer outcomes. Overall I think expectations were applied fairly. For next period, I'd like clearer alignment on upsell ownership between customer success and sales, and a clearer product-request process. Support in the form of enterprise negotiation coaching would make future performance stronger and evaluation clearer.
